examples: Pop a widget, the home page, a dashboard, a Swarm agent chat or a page out of the desktop app and it opens as its own window, listed in the Window menu.
Quit with three pop-outs open, start the app again, and all three come back at their old size and place; one you closed before quitting does not.

Pop a terminal out of the widget menu or a tab menu and its session leaves the main window and opens in a terminal window of its own. Clicking that session in the drawer brings the terminal window forward.
Open two pop-outs, choose Window, Merge All Windows, and they become tabs of one window; Move Tab to New Window pulls one back out. In a browser tab the page shows no title strip at all.

Hide the app with a session scrolling output, then show it: the terminal is already current. With more than 16 terminals open, close a few and the ones that fell back return to the fast renderer when you look at them.
Drag a terminal tab (or a widget header) past the edge of the desktop app window and let go: it opens in a window of its own with the cursor on its title strip, and the terminal keeps running.
how_to: In the desktop app every pop-out button opens a window of its own. Opening the same one again brings the existing window forward.

Choose pop out in a terminal's menu to give a session its own terminal window: the session moves out of the main window, has no drawer or home screen of its own, and shows a short panel (asleep with wake, no longer running with reopen) while it has no live session.
The Window menu lists the open windows and Cmd-backtick cycles through them.
The windows open again after a restart, where they were. A window you closed yourself stays closed.
In a plain browser a pop-out is still a new tab.

Window, Merge All Windows joins windows of the same kind (two pop-outs, say) into one window with a tab bar; Move Tab to New Window splits one out and Show Tab Bar toggles the bar. A pop-out and a terminal window never merge.

Green button or Ctrl-Cmd-F takes a window full screen; Spaces, Mission Control and Stage Manager treat it like any Mac app. The title bar is hidden and the page keeps its top strip clear of the traffic lights; drag that strip to move the window.

A hidden window keeps running, so bringing it back shows it current with no catch-up wait. A terminal that fell back to the plain renderer under load gets its fast renderer back when it is shown and one is free.

Drag a terminal tab or a widget header out past the window edge and release to tear it into its own window at the cursor (Escape cancels). A torn-out terminal leaves the main window's tabs; a widget is copied, as its pop-out is. Closing the torn window leaves the session running. A plain browser does nothing.
media_exempt: native: needs the Electron app and its native windows, which a capture slot does not have
name: Desktop native windows
summary: In the desktop app every pop-out, terminals included, opens as its own native window with its own renderer, listed in the Window menu and brought back with its size and place after a restart, with native tabs per window kind, full screen and a hidden-inset title bar.
where: Any pop-out button in the desktop app; the Window menu in the menu bar.
The pop out item of a terminal's widget menu and tab menu.
Any terminal tab or widget header in the desktop app, dragged past the window edge.
